newsitem.title: UK: Offer says Scottish Power to cut prices.
newsitem.headline: Offer says Scottish Power to cut prices.

text.p: British regulator Offer said on Monday that Scottish Power Plc agreed to reduce prices for its franchise customers by two percent of their total annual bill.
As part of the agreement, Britain's Director General of Electricity Supply, Stephen Littlechild, said he would withdraw his petition for leave to appeal a previous court decision in the dispute.
Scottish Power said it would implement the price cuts for 1997/98 for those customers whose average maximum demand does not exceed 100 kilowatts.
Scottish Power said the proposals would bring its licence into line with that of Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc with regards to how much the utilities can charge customers for electricity.

"We think this is a good solution for everyone," the company said in a statement. "It gives Scottish Power the equality of treatment it has been asking for... and also delivers real benefits to our franchise customers."
The utility's shares slipped 4.0p to 383.5 by 1020 GMT.
